chunks: And Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام used to say:
There is no harm in the leftover water of a mouse when it has drunk from the vessel, that you drink from it or perform wudu (ablution) from it.

key_terms.بِسُؤْرِ: the leftover remnant of a liquid after an animal or person has drunk from it

ai.seo_question: Can water from which a mouse has drunk still be used for drinking or wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling from Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, transmitted through Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding ritual purity. It states that water remaining in a vessel after a mouse has drunk from it may still be used for drinking and for wudu (ablution).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.28 - Ishaq ibn Ammar reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) used to say:
"There is no harm in using the leftover water from which a mouse has drunk, for drinking or performing ablution."
